title: Noisegate rollout scheduler and telemetry annotations (APR 2026) - sketch
body:
Purpose:
Quick operational sketch for the Noisegate feature rollout window. This doc is a thin, actionable checklist + hour-by-hour scheduler for the small-batch canary, plus notes about what telemetry we’ll sample and the precise thresholds that should auto-trigger rollback or escalation.

Context / constraints:
- Feature: Noisegate = dynamic traffic smoothing layer for model routing when live latency spikes exceed guardrails.
- Targets: keep 95th p99 token-latency < 350ms for hosted tier; dedicated regions slightly higher tolerances.
- Window: 2026-04-22 08:00 — 2026-04-25 20:00 PDT (48–72h shepherding, flexible).
- Risk: mis-tuning can cause regional thrashing and eviction storms. Keep conservative traffic ramp.

Quick TL;DR checklist (operators):
- [ ] Preflight: confirm canary build + config applied to staging and a small subset of prod (10% traffic)
- [ ] Smoke: run 10 synthetic traces that exercise long sequences (>512 tokens) and cold KV cache
- [ ] Telemetry boot: enable high-frequency sampling for latencies, queue length, GPU util, tail-latency by model variant
- [ ] Canary ramp schedule configured in orchestration (see Ramp Chart below)
- [ ] Alert hooks wired to PagerDuty escalation (PD: model-routing-oncall)
- [ ] Fallback policy prepared: immediate pin-to-fallback-model variant if p99 > rollback threshold 3x in 15m
- [ ] Docs: customer-visible notes drafted for status page (if we hit rollback)

Ramp chart (compact):
Day 0 (08:00) — 10% traffic baseline
+6h — 25% if no alerts
+24h — 50% if sustained healthy
+48h — 75% if stable and low-error
Full ramp only after manual signoff by release steward and SRE.

Smoke tests (operator commands):
- curl synthetic-runner -> generate 50 sequences (seeded) across 3 regions
- run kv-cache-warmup job (script: infra/tools/kv-warmup.sh)
- compare token-cost delta vs baseline (tool: cost-diff)

Telemetry to capture and thresholds (annotated):
- API p50/p90/p95/p99 latencies (tokens): baseline->compare; rollback if p99 > 3x baseline for two consecutive 5m buckets
- Model error rate (500/502/503) > 0.5% sustained over 10m -> pause ramp and go to investigate
- Queue length (serving runtime) > 75th-percentile plus +30% -> throttle ramping and alert SRE
- GPU util spikes to > 95% for > 5m while latencies worsen -> consider regional capacity fallback
- Customer-impact sample: track requests with >= 2x generation length to ensure long-running tokens are handled

Automated rollback triggers (proposal):
1) p99 latency breach: immediate rollback if p99 > 1000ms for 2 consecutive 5m windows OR 3x baseline as above.
2) Error surge: if 5xx > 1% for 10m -> automatic ramp-down to previous model selector + PD.
3) Resource exhaustion: GPU OOM or node flapping -> immediate cut to safe variant and open incident.

Manual decision points and runbook cues:
- At +6h and +24h, release steward runs a quick health checklist and posts an update to #release-noisegate (use template below).
- If borderline signals, move to a micro-canary (regional isolate) not global.
- Save all telemetry snapshots to the release bucket (s3://redwood-release/noisegate/apr-2026) with tags: steward, canary-step.

Comm templates (quick paste):
- Standup blurb (for #release-noisegate): "Noisegate canary 10% live since 08:00 PDT. Observing p99=280ms, 5xx=0.04%. Next ramp to 25% at 14:00 if green."
- Incident short: "Rollback executed at 14:18 PDT due to p99 latency spike >1000ms. Traffic pinned to v-2026-04-19-fallback. Postmortem TBD."

Post-rollout validation (what we check before closing):
- Full smoke run at full traffic (if we reached full) and synthetic diffusion test across region boundaries.
- Cost delta analysis: ensure per-token compute cost within 10% of projected.
- Quality sampling: run 200 random prompts through golden evaluation set; compare BLEU/QA heuristics to baseline.
- Open a short retro doc (template linked_artifacts) and assign action items.

Open questions / TODOs (notes to self):
- Should the rollback threshold be tightened for APAC regions due to higher variance? (Priya to advise)
- Confirm PD escalation order: primary is runtime-sre, secondary is model-serving-eng.
- Need a quick-label pipeline for telemetry snapshots (Jonah)

Attachments / local references:
- tiny checklist file: ./ops/rollout-mini-checklist.md (copy into the runbook binder)
- perf curves: uploads in GH PR above (infra/pull/1287)

If you’re reading this and prepping the run: call out any external customer pilot groups before ramping beyond 25%. Keep the window quiet and conservative.

Endnotes: this is intentionally lightweight — use the larger release-dossier if we convert Noisegate to a full-product rollout.

-- Maya
